title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Policy
scope: This policy applies to suspected or confirmed cybersecurity events affecting organizational systems, information, personnel, customers, suppliers, or services.
principles: The organization prepares for incidents before they occur and maintains clear decision rights for time-sensitive actions.
Reports are triaged using consistent severity criteria, preserving facts and limiting unnecessary disclosure.
Containment, eradication, recovery, and communications decisions are documented with accountable owners and timestamps.
Every material incident produces lessons that improve risk treatment, controls, and response capability.

requirements.statement: The organization must maintain an incident response plan, contact roster, severity model, and tested escalation paths.
Potential incidents must be recorded in the case system with reporter, time observed, affected asset, initial facts, and assigned triage owner.
Severity must consider business impact, data sensitivity, scope, legal or regulatory exposure, customer impact, and threat confidence.
Evidence must be preserved with chain-of-custody details when an incident may require legal, regulatory, employment, or contractual action.
Containment and recovery actions must be authorized according to severity, recorded in the case, and validated before closure.
Material incidents must trigger documented internal, customer, supplier, legal, or regulatory communications according to approved notification criteria.
Post-incident review must identify root contributing factors, control improvements, owners, deadlines, and whether residual risk acceptance is required.

exceptions.compensating_control: Record the emergency decision in the case and schedule a retrospective approval review.
Document why a notification criterion could not be met and preserve the decision evidence.
